title: Affine sections preserve the structure-algebra ring pushout
statement: Let $f:U\to X$ be affine, $A=f_*\mathcal O_U$, $r_0:f^{-1}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_U$ the structure map, and $t_0=f^{-1}\rho$ for $\rho:\mathcal O_X\to A$. Suppose $b:\mathcal O_U\to B$ and $t:f^{-1}A\to B$ form a pushout of $r_0,t_0$ in commutative ring sheaves. For an affine open $V\subseteq X$, set $W=f^{-1}V$, $D=\Gamma(X,V)$, $C=\Gamma(U,W)$, and $\delta=t_W\circ\eta_{A,V}:C\to B(W)$, where $\eta_A$ is the ring inverse-image/direct-image unit. Then the square in commutative rings with both upper maps $f^\sharp_V:D\to C$, lower left map $b_W:C\to B(W)$, and lower right map $\delta:C\to B(W)$ is a pushout.

source.place: Tag 01SB, proof: elucidation and affine reduction; with Schemes Tags 01I9, 01IA and 01HV for affine pullback sections

proof.text: For A=f_*O_U, the restricted-scalar regular A-module is f_*O_U as an O_X-module. It is quasi-coherent since affine f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and O_U is quasi-coherent.

Specialize pushout scalar-extension cancellation to the regular A-module. Inverse image of the regular module is the regular inverse-image algebra module, and extending it along t is the regular B-module by x tensor a ↦ x*t(a), with inverse x ↦ x tensor 1. The comparison identifies this module with tensor pullback of the restricted-scalar A-module, with its canonical unit.

The inverse image W of affine V is affine. Apply the affine module sections comparison and swap tensor factors: B(W) is C tensor_D C. The unit comparison gives 1 tensor d ↦ δ(d); first-factor scalar linearity gives c tensor d ↦ b(c)δ(d). These maps are multiplicative since they are the ring-tensor comparison before sheafification, and that comparison respects the sheafification unit. Hence the section comparison is a ring isomorphism respecting both ring legs.
Transport CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct through that ring isomorphism. This yields exactly the section ring pushout stated here, including the zero ring and empty open.
